source: A supplement to the Papyrus of Ani, which does not have this passage. In other papyri of the Theban Book of the Dead, Spell 125 continues after the 42 declarations with this address to the gods; the text is Budge's footnote on p. 203: 'For the text see Naville, Todtenbuch, Bd. I., Bll. 137, 138' — the Appendix is supplied from Naville's 1886 edition of the Theban Book of the Dead (vol. I, plates 137–138), not from the Papyrus of Ani; no other footnote in pp. 203–213 names a papyrus. Hieroglyphs transcribed from the Appendix that E. A. W. Budge prints at this point in The Book of the Dead: The Papyrus of Ani in the British Museum (London, 1895), pp. 203–213 (Appendix); his transliteration and word-by-word English were used to check the reading of the signs and the sense, never for wording. Transliteration in the Leiden convention, with the reed written i; translation made fresh from the Egyptian. The line under each word ("say") is the conventional Egyptological classroom pronunciation, an artificial teaching pronunciation. The grouping of signs within a word follows Budge's type.
about: Ani's papyrus ends Spell 125 with the 42 declarations of innocence and goes straight on to other spells; other papyri of the Theban Book of the Dead continue here with this address to the gods of the hall. The dead person greets the judges, says what good they have done, and is then questioned at the door of the Hall of the Two Truths: each part of the door, and the floor, will let them pass only if they can say its secret name, until Thoth announces them to Osiris and they are given bread and beer. It is given from the text Budge prints in his Appendix, taken from Naville's 1886 edition; it is not on Ani's papyrus.

sentences.l: hail · to-face · your · gods · these
sentences.i: Hail to you, you gods here!
sentences.n: ind ḥr·ṯn is the greeting 'hail to you': ind is the reed i, the sign nḏ (an uncertain object, perhaps a spindle) with the cobra ḏ as its complement, and the papyrus roll as classifier — it grew from i 'O' and nḏ ḥr 'greet the face'. ḥr 'face' is the face with stroke (a second stroke follows it), and ·ṯn 'your' (plural, for the gods are many) is written here in its older form, tethering-rope ṯ, water n and plural strokes; elsewhere in this text it is loaf t, n and strokes, ·tn. nṯrw 'gods' is the flag nṯr three times, and ipw 'these' (reed i, stool p, quail chick w, stroke) is the plural demonstrative, pointing at the gods present. The address is supplied by Budge from Naville's text of other papyri, where the dead man goes on to speak to the gods of the hall after the 42 declarations.

sentences.i: I know you; I know your names.
sentences.n: iw·i (reed i, quail chick w, seated man ·i) opens the statement: 'I'. rḫ·kwi is the stative of rḫ 'know' (mouth r, placenta ḫ, the papyrus roll for an abstract) with the 1st-person ending ·kwi, written here k, a stroke and w (the print sets the stroke and the chick side by side, so the order of the two is not meaningful); the stative of rḫ means 'I know', the knowledge being a state. Budge prints rḫ·kwi and the following tn as one group; they are split here, for tn (loaf t, water n, plural strokes) is a word of its own, the dependent pronoun 'you' (plural), object of the verb. The second rḫ·kwi has the same spelling with chick and stroke in the usual order. rn 'name' (mouth r, water n) is followed by a man with his hand to his mouth, which the print gives where a name-classifier might stand, and a stroke; no plural is written, but the gods are many and 'your names' is meant. To know a being's name is to have power over it: the claim opens the plea.

sentences.n: nn (water n written twice) is the negative of the future: nn + sḏm·f, 'I shall not …'. ḫr·i is ḫr 'fall' (placenta ḫ, mouth r) with ·i; its classifier is printed as a cord with crossing ends (coded V12), not the falling man the verb usually takes, and the sign is doubtful. n is the preposition 'to'. šꜥt 'slaughter, the slaughtering' is pool š (the print's sign is an approximation), arm ꜥ and loaf t, with a spiky sign (coded M44, approximate) and the knife as classifiers and plural strokes; then ·tn 'your'. sentences.i: You will not report my wrong to this god whom you follow.
sentences.n: Another nn + sḏm·f: 'you will not …'. sꜥr is the causative of ꜥr 'go up': 'make go up', that is, bring a matter up to a superior, report it; it is the folded cloth s, arm ꜥ and mouth r, with a sign the print gives like a balance (coded U38, approximate) — fitting for a report that is to be weighed. The text writes b-i with the sparrow; read bin 'evil, wrong': the n is left out (Budge restores it in his transliteration but nothing stands for it in the signs). ·i 'my'. n nṯr pn 'to this god': pn 'this' (stool p, water n) follows its noun. nty ṯn m-ḫt·f 'whom you follow', literally 'who you (are) in his following': nty is the relative 'who', ṯn the dependent pronoun 'you' in its older spelling with ṯ, and m-ḫt 'after, in the train of' is owl m, the tree ḫt with ḫ and t as complements and the walking legs, + ·f. 'This god' is presumably the judge of the hall.

sentences.l: not · come · case · my · before · you
sentences.i: My case will not come before you.
sentences.n: nn again, with iw 'come' (the walking legs as word-sign with w as complement, as in the introduction). A loaf t follows the verb, and it is not clear what it is: if nn stands here for the single n, as later copies often write it, iwt would be the sḏmt·f, 'my case has not yet come before you'; it could also be a slip for the impersonal ·tw. It is translated with nn as written, as the future. sp 'occasion, case' (bolt s, stool p) here means a deed charged against the speaker; its classifier is printed as the sun-disc, not the threshing-floor sp normally takes (and has on line 6), and the word is read sp either way. ḥr·tn 'before you, to you' is the face ḥr with r as complement and ·tn.

sentences.i: Hail to you, you gods who are in your Hall of the Two Truths, who have no falsehood in their bodies,
sentences.n: The greeting of line 2 again, now with ·tn written loaf t, water n, plural strokes. The text writes reed i with the crossed planks im; read imyw 'who are in' (the nisba of m 'in'), its plural ending not written. wsḫt 'hall' is quail chick w (ahead of its sign), the cup wsḫ, loaf t and the house as classifier, with ·ṯn 'your' in the older spelling (no ḫ is written beside the cup). nt 'of' (n + t) is the feminine genitive, agreeing with wsḫt; mꜣꜥti 'the Two Truths' is sickle, arm, loaf t, two strokes y and the feather of Maat twice. The text writes water n, t, vulture ꜣ, the sparrow and plural strokes; read iwty 'who have no …', the negative relative (Budge: àt 'without'). On line 18 the same word is written with the spread arms (D35) for iwt, t, the vulture standing for -y and the sparrow; here the water n stands in for the arms, which are also read n. The reading is probable, not certain. The text writes g-r; read grg 'falsehood, lie': the second g is not written, unless the stick-sign that follows (coded T14, approximate) stands for it. ẖt·sn 'their bodies': ẖt 'belly, body' is the belly-and-teats sign ẖ with t and strokes, then ·sn 'their' (bolt s, water n, strokes).

sentences.l: who-live · on · truth · in · Heliopolis · who-swallow · of · innards(?) · their · before · Horus · who-is-in · disk · his
sentences.i: who live on truth in Heliopolis, who swallow their innards(?) in the presence of Horus who is in his disk:
sentences.n: ꜥnḫyw 'who live' is the plural participle of ꜥnḫ: the ankh-sign ꜥnḫ, two reeds y, quail chick w and stroke. ꜥnḫ m 'live on' (food): the gods feed on truth (mꜣꜥt spelled out as on line 5). iwnw 'Heliopolis' is the pillar iwn, the pot nw and the town sign. sꜥmyw 'who swallow' (bolt s, arm ꜥ, owl m, two reeds y, chick w) is another plural participle; sꜥm is 'swallow, gulp down', and its classifiers are a horned head on a pole (coded F1, approximate) and the man with hand to mouth, for eating. sꜥm m is 'swallow (some) of'. What they swallow is doubtful: ḥꜣwt (the papyrus clump ḥꜣ with ꜣ, t, w) has the coiled intestine (coded F46, approximate) and plural strokes as classifiers, so 'innards' is meant, + ·sn 'their'; Budge's 'entrails' rests on the same sign. Whose innards — the gods' own, or the wicked's — the text does not say. m-bꜣḥ as on line 5. Horus is the falcon with the seated god; imy 'who is in' (reed i, crossed planks im), and itn·f 'his disk' (i, t, n, the sun-disc, ·f): the sun's disk, here Horus as the sun.

sentences.n: rdi·n·i 'I have given' (mouth r, the arm giving di — printed without its loaf — the n of the past, ·i). t 'bread' is the loaf t with a long loaf and a cup holding a cone of bread (coded W10, approximate) as classifiers, and strokes. n 'to'. Budge prints ḏd·tw and n·f 'to him' as one group; they are split here. n·f is the preposition n with ·f: the text now speaks of the dead man in the third person. iy wy 'how welcome!': iy 'come' (reed-leaf ii, two strokes y, walking legs) with the particle wy (chick w, two strokes y) that exclaims over a quality — 'how come (you are)!'. sp sn, the threshing-floor sp and the numeral 2, means 'twice': the word before it is to be said twice. in 'by' names the speakers: mꜣꜣyw 'those who see' (sickle mꜣ, the eye, vulture ꜣ, two reeds y, chick w, stroke), the plural participle of mꜣꜣ, with sw 'him' (the sedge sw with w), the dependent pronoun as object.

sentences.i: For I heard that word which the donkey spoke with the cat in the house of Heped-ra(?).
sentences.n: The dead man speaks again. ḥr-ntt 'because', as on line 6. sḏm·n·i 'I heard' is the ear sḏm with owl m as complement, the n of the sḏm·n·f and ·i. The printed signs are the staff md, hand d, t, the man with hand to mouth and stroke: mdt 'word, speech' (Budge's transliteration, t'eṭet, does not match them). twy 'that' (t, w, two reeds) is the feminine demonstrative, agreeing with mdt. ḏdt (cobra ḏ, hand d, t) is the relative form 'which … spoke', and its subject follows directly: 'which the donkey spoke'; Budge's transliteration line adds a word 'by' with no sign above it, and nothing is read for it. ꜥꜣ 'donkey' is the column ꜥꜣ with the donkey as classifier; between them stands the phallus-like sign of m-bꜣḥ, which has no evident part in the word and is taken as a second classifier. ḥnꜥ 'with' (wick ḥ, water n, arm ꜥ); miw 'cat' (the milk-jug mi with i, w, the cat). pr 'house' with its stroke. The god's name is wick ḥ, stool p, hand d, the crossed sticks, mouth r with stroke and the seated god; read ḥpd-rꜣ, perhaps 'Open of Mouth' (ḥpd 'open (the mouth)' + rꜣ 'mouth'), but the name is not known elsewhere and its reading is uncertain. What the donkey and the cat said is not told; it was a word the speaker could repeat, and so a proof that he had been there.

sentences.i: As for me, I make my report before the gods, knowing what concerns their persons.
sentences.n: Here a new address begins in Naville's text. ink 'I' is the independent pronoun: the nw-pot (in), the basket (k) and the seated man as classifier. It stands at the head of the sentence for emphasis, 'I, I …'. smi·i 'I report' is from smi 'report, make petition'. The signs are the folded cloth s; a sign printed as three reeds on a slab (coded M20, approximate), standing for sm; the owl m as complement; two strokes for i; a w; the man with his hand to his mouth (speech); and ·i, the seated man, 'I', the 1st person suffix. The w has no place in the verb form, and with it the group could also be the noun 'my reports'. The second sign is not secure either. m-bꜣḥ 'in the presence of' is the owl m with the phallus sign bꜣḥ and its stroke. nṯrw 'gods' writes the god's flag three times for the plural. rḫ 'knowing' (mouth r, placenta ḫ, papyrus roll) has no ending and is taken as describing the speaker. ẖrt 'what belongs to, concerns' is the butcher's block ẖr with r, t and two classifiers. ẖt 'body' (the belly sign ẖ with t) here means the gods' persons. ·sn 'their', the 3rd person plural suffix, is the bolt s with water n and plural strokes.

sentences.i: I have come here to bear witness to what is right.
sentences.n: ii·n·i 'I have come' is the sḏm·n·f, the form for a completed action. It is the verb ii (the reed-leaf ii, a reed i and the walking legs), then the n that marks the form, then ·i. ꜥꜣ, the column, is read as the adverb 'here, hither', as in the introduction's ii·n·i ꜥꜣ. Under it the print sets the same balance-like sign as in sꜥr on line 4 (coded U38, approximate). It has no clear place here and is taken as a classifier, so the reading is doubtful (Budge: 'advancing'). r + infinitive gives the purpose. smtr is the bolt s, the phallus sign mt, t, mouth r, two strokes and the man with his hand to his mouth. It is the causative of mtr 'bear witness', 'examine, testify', and the two strokes are not read. mꜣꜥt, Maat, 'what is right, truth', is written here with sickle mꜣ, arm ꜥ, t, the papyrus roll and a stroke, without the plinth.

sentences.i: May I be saved from those messengers of yours who inflict harm and bring about punishments(?), whose faces are uncovered,
sentences.n: nḥm 'take away, rescue' is water n, the bowl ḥm with m as complement, and the low sign printed U15 for the forearm with stick, the classifier of force. Here it carries ·kwi (k, w and the seated man), the ending of the stative for 'I': 'I am saved'. The stative is now and then used for a wish (most often in the 2nd person), and 'may I be saved' is taken so here; Budge takes it as a command, 'deliver me'. m-ꜥ 'from (the hand of)' is the owl m joined to the arm ꜥ. nꜣy·k (water n, vulture ꜣ, two reeds, plural strokes, the basket ·k) is the possessive article of later Egyptian, 'your'. The n after it is the genitive 'of' and is not needed in English. wpwtyw 'messengers' is the horns wp (coded F13, approximate) with p, w and t, then the vulture apparently standing for the ending -y (as in iwty below), crossed sticks, a second t, the papyrus roll and plural strokes. wddyw (w, two hands d, two reeds, crossed sticks, w, stroke) is read as the imperfective participle of wdi 'put, cast, inflict' (the doubled d is its gemination), which is not certain. ṯmsw 'harm, injuries' is the tethering rope ṯ and the fox-skins ms with s and w, then classifiers including the bad bird. It is a rare word, and the identifications of its first sign and classifiers are approximate. sḫpryw 'who bring about' is the causative of ḫpr 'come into being': s, the scarab ḫpr, r, two reeds, stroke and w. idryt (reed i, hand d, mouth r, two reeds, t, a plant coded M2 (approximate) and the papyrus roll) is not otherwise known to this edition. 'Punishments, afflictions' follows the sense and Budge's 'calamities'. iwty 'who has not, without' is the negative relative: the spread arms (D35), t, the vulture for -y and the bad bird. ṯꜣmt 'covering, veil' is the duckling ṯꜣ with ꜣ, m, t, a fringed cloth (approximate) and the U15 sign. nt is the feminine form of the genitive, agreeing with it. ḥrw·sn 'their faces' is the face with two strokes and ·sn.

sentences.n: The same words, now from another part of the door. The negation is written with one n this time, not nn. Strictly, n with a sḏm·f is 'I do not (cannot) let'; in a refrain repeated word for word it is more likely nn written short, and it is translated as before. ꜥryt (arm ꜥ, mouth r, two reeds for y, t, and the wood classifier) is the part of the door Budge calls the lintel; ꜥryt can be the frame or entrance of a door in general, and which piece is meant is not certain. sentences.n: The dead person answers with a question. Budge gives no English for ḥr m ir·f; it is read here as ḥr m 'for what? why?' — the preposition ḥr with the interrogative m, written with the same owl-and-forearm ligature as mi 'come' — and irf (reed, mouth, horned viper), the particle 'then' that often follows a question, as on line 25. grt (stand g, r, t, and a man with hand to mouth as classifier) is taken with Budge as gr 'be silent', the classifier pointing to the mouth; the same three signs also write the particle grt 'now, moreover', so 'I, moreover, am pure' is possible. Silence and purity are the virtues the dead claims at the judgement.

sentences.l: Besu · before · Min · (is) · the-name · of · leg · my · right
sentences.i: 'Besu-before-Min' is the name of my right leg.
sentences.n: The dead person answers the floor of the hall, which has asked the names of the legs that tread on it. The answer is a sentence of two nouns side by side, 'A (is) the name of B', as at the door. bsw is foot b, folded cloth s, quail chick w, with a fish as classifier and plural strokes; the fish cannot be identified in the type (coded K1, an approximation) and the word is not clear. It may belong with bs 'bring in, introduce', but a fish fits no known sense, and it is left as a name, Besu. m-bꜣḥ 'before, in the presence of' is the owl m and the phallus bꜣḥ with its stroke; the flat roll-like sign under it (coded Y1, the papyrus roll) is written in every m-bꜣḥ of this text (as on line 5). mnw is Min, the god of Coptos and Akhmim, written with his emblem and the seated god (Budge: Amsu, his old reading of the emblem). rd·i 'my leg' is mouth r, hand d, the leg as classifier and the seated man ·i 'my'. imny 'right' is the feather on its standard, the sign of the West, which also writes the word for 'right' (the West lies on the right hand of one who faces south, as Egyptians oriented themselves), with m as complement and the strokes y: the same group as imnt on the right lintel, read the same way (Budge reads unem; wnmy is another word for 'right', but the West sign with m points to imn); the last sign, a stroke ending in a loop, is the classifier and is only approximated by its code (V1).

sentences.i: Tread on us, then, for you know us.
sentences.n: The floor gives way. ḫnd 'tread, step' is placenta ḫ, water n, hand d, with a leg and the walking legs as classifiers: the bare stem is the imperative. ir·k, written reed–mouth–basket, is the preposition r with ·k after an imperative, 'you, then', as at the end of Anubis's speech in the introduction. ḥr·n 'upon us': the face ḥr with r and its stroke, and ·n 'us' (water n with plural strokes, the 1st person plural). iw·k rḫ·ṯi 'you know': iw with ·k, and the stative of rḫ 'know' (mouth r, placenta ḫ, papyrus roll) with the 2nd singular ending written in its older form ṯi (the tethering rope ṯ and reed i). sentences.n: nn (water n written twice) is the negative of the future: nn smi·i 'I will not announce'. smi 'report, announce' is folded cloth s and the lung-and-windpipe sign (here for sm), reed i, the man with hand to mouth (speech) and ·i 'I'; tw (loaf t, quail chick w) is the dependent pronoun 'you', the object. in N after a speech is 'says N'. iry-ꜥꜣ 'doorkeeper', literally 'the one belonging to the door', joins two of Budge's groups as one word: the guardian figure for iry (coded A47, an approximation of a wrapped man with a stick), then ꜥꜣ 'door', the column ꜥꜣ over a hatched door-leaf (coded O31 as the nearest sign) and the branch of wood. wsḫt 'hall' is the hall-plan alone; ṯn is the feminine 'this' in its older form with ṯ. n-is (water n, reed i, folded cloth s) is 'unless, except' (n 'not' + the particle is), followed by the sḏm·n·f ḏd·n·k 'you have said': ḏd 'say' (cobra, hand), the n that marks the completed action, ·k 'you'.

sentences.i: 'He who discerns hearts and searches bodies' is your name.
sentences.n: Two participles, each with its object, make the doorkeeper's name. siꜣ 'perceive, discern' is the fringed cloth siꜣ (the type's sign is doubtful, coded S32) with ꜣ as complement and the man with hand to mouth; ibw 'hearts' is the heart-jar ib with its stroke and plural strokes. ḏꜥr 'search out, investigate' is cobra ḏ, arm ꜥ, mouth r, a thin stroke (coded Z1, perhaps another stroke) and the walking legs. ẖt 'belly, body' is the belly-with-teats sign ẖ with t and plural strokes, 'bellies': the inner self, as the heart is (Budge: 'reins', the inner organs). The heart and the belly were where a person's thoughts and deeds were thought to lie, and the judge of the dead looks into both.

sentences.n: in (water n alone again) answers the question in the same form: 'it is …'. The first sign of the next word is not clear in the type: a broad arch with a small ring on top, coded W19 (the jug in its net, mi) as the nearest; then vulture ꜣ, quail chick w, and the man with hand to mouth and the seated man as classifiers — a man known by what he says. sentences.n: ḫw 'protect, guard' is written with the same signs as ḫww 'evil' above, with the papyrus roll; then n and ·i: the sḏm·n·f 'I have protected (myself)'. sentences.n: nm in 'who is it that …' as before, with a participle: hꜣt (courtyard h, two vultures ꜣ, loaf t, walking legs) is from hꜣi 'go down'; the t is unexpected, and the form is not certain. sḏt 'flame, fire' is taken from the crossed sticks (here for sḏ), t and a flame-like sign (coded Q7); Budge reads seśet. inbwt·s 'its walls': reed and fish in with n as complement, b, w, t, the wall and a canal-like sign (coded N23, an approximation) as classifiers, plural strokes, and ·s 'its' (the folded cloth s, the feminine suffix: the flame's walls). m iꜥrwt 'of uraei': iꜥrt is the uraeus, the rearing cobra of the royal brow (reed, arm, mouth, t, w, cobra, plural), so the walls are living fire-spitting snakes. wnnw sꜣtw·f 'his floor being …': wnn 'be' (hare wn, n, n, the pot, w, plural strokes) and sꜣtw 'ground, floor' (pintail sꜣ, t, w, canal-sign, plural strokes, house and stroke), with ·f 'his', the one who goes down; the form of wnn is not certain (the w may be the ending of the prospective sḏm·f), and the clause is taken as circumstantial. nn 'these' (water n, the adze nw, approximated, and the pot nw) is the demonstrative before its noun, spelled as in 'these lands of the Fenkhu' on line 23; Budge too reads a demonstrative ('that same'). The same signs could spell Nu (Nun), the primeval water, but the god's classifiers are missing, and the word order would not give 'the waters of Nu'. The last word, quail chick w and two reeds with three water-lines, a pool and the canal-sign, is a word for a body of water that cannot be identified; Budge takes it as 'lake'. The whole question is obscure.

sentences.i: He has decreed it (?) for me.
sentences.n: Budge leaves the first group untransliterated, printing dots, though his English has 'Hath decreed it'. It is a staff with a loop at its foot crossed by a horned viper, then two strokes: the staff is taken as the cord-on-stick wḏ 'command, decree' (coded V25, an approximation), the viper as ·f 'he' (the sḏm·f), and the two strokes are not explained. sw (sedge, w) is then the dependent pronoun 'it', the object, and r·i (mouth r, seated man) 'for me' or 'concerning me'. 'He' is perhaps Thoth or Osiris; the sentence is doubtful in reading and sense. These are the last words of the address in the papyrus Budge follows.

glossary.wḏꜥ: wḏꜥ — to judge, separate (verb); wḏꜥ(w)t 'judgement, decision' (noun)
glossary.psš: psš — to divide, split, share out (verb); division, splitting (noun)
glossary.išd: išd — the persea tree, sacred tree of Heliopolis (noun)
glossary.ẖnw: ẖnw — the inside, interior, residence (noun; m ẖnw 'within')
glossary.rꜣ-sṯꜣw: rꜣ-sṯꜣw — Rosetau, the Sokar necropolis realm near Giza
glossary.ẖrt: ẖrt — what belongs to someone, affairs, concerns; possessions (noun)
glossary.smtr: smtr — to examine, question; to bear witness (verb; causative of mtr 'be witness')

glossary.twr: twr — to be clean, pure; to cleanse, purify (verb)

glossary.ẖry: ẖry — lower, who/which is beneath (nisba of ẖr)
glossary.ḥꜣyt: ḥꜣyt — some plant or thicket (noun; sense uncertain; Budge: 'flowers')
glossary.bꜣq: bꜣq — the moringa tree, which gives ben-oil (noun; Budge: 'olive')
glossary.ḥr-ꜥ: ḥr-ꜥ — at once, forthwith (adverb; lit. 'upon the arm')
glossary.pty: pty — who? what? (interrogative pronoun; pty tr 'who/what then?')
glossary.im: im — there, therein (adverb; nty im "he who is there")

glossary.ihhy: ihhy — rejoicing, jubilation, the cry of joy (noun)
glossary.tꜣ: tꜣ — to be hot; tꜣ-ib 'hot-tempered' · a second word of the same spelling: land, earth (noun; plural tꜣw 'lands'; dual tꜣwy 'the Two Lands', Egypt; tp tꜣ 'upon earth')

glossary.sḏt: sḏt — fire, flame (noun; written with the crossed sticks, sḏ)
glossary.wꜣḏ: wꜣḏ — papyrus stem; papyrus-column, papyrus-sceptre or amulet (noun) · also green, fresh, flourishing (adjective; verb wꜣḏ 'be green') (Budge: 'tablet')
glossary.ṯḥnt: ṯḥnt — faience, glazed ware; something gleaming (noun; Budge: 'crystal')

glossary.wḏb: wḏb — riverbank, shore; the land along the river (noun)
glossary.wꜣs: wꜣs — the was-sceptre, a staff with an animal head and forked foot (noun)
glossary.šd: šd — to take, take away, take out; to rescue; to recite, read out (verb)
glossary.irf: irf — then, now (enclitic particle, from r + ·f; mostly in questions, 'what then?', also after a statement or a command)
glossary.pꜣ: pꜣ — the (masculine definite article of later Egyptian; fem. tꜣ, plural nꜣ)
glossary.hꜣtw: hꜣtw — to cry out, utter (?) (verb; a word not otherwise known, written with the man with hand to mouth; Budge: 'uttered words')
glossary.sd: sd — to break (verb; a writing of sḏ 'break', with the hand d for the cobra ḏ)
glossary.qmꜣ: qmꜣ — to create, produce, bring forth (verb)

glossary.tn: tn — this (feminine demonstrative, after its noun; masculine pn)

glossary.·n: ·n — we, us, our (1st person plural suffix pronoun; water sign with plural strokes)
glossary.bnš: bnš — a part of a door, perhaps the bolt or the jamb (noun; reading and sense not secure; Budge: benś)

glossary.tḫ: tḫ — plummet, the weight hanging from the beam of the balance (noun)
glossary.bw: bw — place (noun; bw mꜣꜥ "what is right", lit. "the place of right")
glossary.·t: ·t — you, your (2nd person feminine singular suffix pronoun; the bread-loaf sign)
glossary.ꜥryt: ꜥryt — door-frame, entrance; a part of the doorway, perhaps the lintel or a jamb (noun; Budge: ārit)
glossary.imny: imny — right, on the right hand; western (nisba adjective; fem. imnt; written with the emblem of the West)
glossary.ḥnk: ḥnk — to present, offer (verb); ḥnkw, ḥnkt "what is presented, offering" (noun)
glossary.fꜣt: fꜣt — load, burden, what is carried (noun; from fꜣi "carry, lift")
glossary.iꜣby: iꜣby — left, on the left hand; eastern (nisba adjective; fem. iꜣbt; written with the emblem of the East)
glossary.sš: sš — scribe (noun; the palette-and-pen sign) · a second word of the same spelling: to pass, go through (verb; doubtful here)
glossary.gb: gb — Geb, god of the earth (god's name; Budge: Seb)
glossary.wn: wn — to open (verb; wn n "open to")

glossary.pꜣyt: pꜣyt — a part of a door, perhaps a bar or lock (noun; sense not secure; Budge: pait)

glossary.sbk: sbk — Sobek, the crocodile god (god's name; Budge: Sebek)
glossary.bꜣḫw: bꜣḫw — Bakhu, the mountain of the sunrise in the east (place name; Budge: Baχau)
glossary.iry: iry — one who belongs to, keeper of (nisba of r "to"; iry ꜥꜣ "doorkeeper")
glossary.qbt: qbt — a part of the body (?) (noun; reading and sense uncertain; Budge: qebt 'arm')
glossary.sꜣ: sꜣ — protection (noun; m sꜣ "for the protection of")
glossary.wsir: wsir — Osiris, god of the dead and king of the world below; Wsir N "the Osiris N", the dead person (god's name; Budge: Àusàr)
glossary.ḥpt: ḥpt — door-post, jamb (?) (noun; plural ḥptw; sense not secure; Budge: ḥeptu)
glossary.rnnwtt: rnnwtt — Renenutet, cobra goddess of harvest and nourishment (god's name; Budge: Rennut)
glossary.gr: gr — to be silent, still (verb) · a second word of nearly the same spelling: the particle grt 'now, moreover, indeed'

glossary.mnw: mnw — Min, the ithyphallic god of fertility and of the desert roads, lord of Coptos and Akhmim (god's name; Budge: Àmsu)
glossary.wnpt: wnpt — a feminine noun written with the wood classifier, perhaps a wooden object; not otherwise known (noun; reading and sense uncertain; Budge: un pet "grief")
glossary.nbt-ḥwt: nbt-ḥwt — Nephthys, "Lady of the Mansion", sister of Isis, Osiris and Seth, a mourner of Osiris (goddess's name; Budge: Nebt-ḥet)
glossary.iry-ꜥꜣ: iry-ꜥꜣ — doorkeeper, porter (noun; lit. "the one belonging to the door": iry + ꜥꜣ "door, door-leaf")
glossary.siꜣ: siꜣ — to perceive, recognise, discern (verb); Sia, the god of perception
glossary.ḏꜥr: ḏꜥr — to search out, investigate, examine (verb)
glossary.mꜣw: mꜣw — Mau(?), a title of Thoth, in the phrase mꜣw tꜣwy 'the Mau of the Two Lands' (title; reading and sense uncertain; Budge: māau 'recorder')
glossary.ḏḥwty: ḏḥwty — Thoth, the ibis god of writing, reckoning and wisdom, recorder of the judgement of the dead (god's name; Budge: Teḥuti)
glossary.ḫrt: ḫrt — condition, state, affairs; what belongs to one (noun)
glossary.ḫww: ḫww — evil, wrongdoing (noun; written with the bird of bad things)
glossary.šnt: šnt — hostility, harmful acts, strife (noun; cf. šnṯ "revile, quarrel"; reading uncertain; Budge: śentet)
glossary.twi: twi — I, me (1st person singular pronoun; later form of the dependent wi)
glossary.m-m: m-m — among, in the midst of (compound preposition; later spelled with ꜥ)
glossary.inb: inb — wall (noun; plural inbw, also inbwt)
glossary.iꜥrt: iꜥrt — uraeus, the rearing cobra on the brow of gods and kings (noun; plural iꜥrwt)
glossary.wnn: wnn — to be, exist (verb; wn·n·i "I have been"; n wn "there is not")
glossary.sbi: sbi — to go, pass, travel (verb; participle sby "one who passes")
glossary.wḏꜣ: wḏꜣ — to proceed, go on, set out (verb)
glossary.pri: pri — to go out, come forth (verb)
